title: MCPStdioClient never drains subprocess stderr
description: start() creates the subprocess with stderr=PIPE but nothing ever reads it. A chatty MCP server fills the pipe buffer and deadlocks the bridge. Either drain stderr into the logger or stop piping it.
close_reason: Background stderr drain task added in 77b3a68 with a reproducing regression test

title: MCPStdioClient drops server-initiated requests and notifications
description: _read_response discards any message whose id does not match the pending request id. MCP servers can call back into the client (sampling/createMessage, roots/list, elicitation/create) and send notifications; those are silently dropped. Blocks real bidirectional MCP client support.
close_reason: Background read loop routes responses, server requests, and notifications in 7114a96

title: Support runtime-configured MCP servers via session/new mcpServers
description: python-acp currently binds ONE MCP server at startup via --mcp-command in cli.py, shared by all WebSocket clients. ACP v1 has the client pass mcpServers in session/new, making the agent an MCP client to N per-session servers. Needs a connection registry keyed by session, replacing the single MCPStdioClient held by ACPWebSocketBridge.

title: Make the Makefile venv handling correct both in an activated venv and on a bare CI runner
description:
The Makefile assumes one environment shape and silently does the wrong thing in the other.

Local (this sandbox and any developer who has run 'source venv/bin/activate'): VIRTUAL_ENV=/Users/dave/dev/other/python-acp/venv and PATH starts with venv/bin, so the Makefile's 'PYTHON ?= python3' resolves to venv/bin/python3 -- the interpreter inside the venv make is about to manage. VENV_DIR resolves to 'venv' because that directory exists.

GitHub Actions (all four legs of the ci.yml matrix added in pyacp-0f6): a fresh checkout has neither .venv nor venv, so VENV_DIR falls through to '.venv', no venv is active, and 'python3' is whatever actions/setup-python put on PATH.

Concrete defects that follow:

1. 'make venv' never recreates an existing venv -- the recipe is guarded by 'if [ ! -d $(VENV_DIR) ]'. So 'make venv PYTHON=python3.12' on a machine that already has venv/ built from 3.14 does not build a 3.12 environment; it pip-installs into the 3.14 one and reports success. There is no supported way to reproduce a non-default matrix leg locally. Validating pyacp-0f6 required building .venv311/.venv312/.venv313 by hand, entirely outside the Makefile, precisely because of this.

2. VENV_DIR differs between the two environments ('venv' locally, '.venv' in CI) purely as a side effect of which directory happens to exist. Two developers on the same commit can be using different directories, and neither matches CI.

3. Every target depends on venv, and the venv recipe unconditionally runs 'pip install --upgrade pip' followed by 'pip install -e .[dev]'. So 'make test' always reaches the network. In a network-restricted sandbox that is a hard failure (pip cannot verify the proxy's TLS cert against Python's CA store, so make venv exits non-zero before any test runs); in CI it is wasted time on every invocation.

4. DEMO_MCP_COMMAND defaults to bare 'python3 tests/fixtures/mock_mcp_server.py' rather than $(PYTHON_BIN). 'make run' therefore launches the MCP subprocess on whatever python3 is on PATH while the bridge itself runs on $(VENV_DIR)/bin/python. Those coincide only when a venv is already activated -- exactly the local case, which is why it has never been noticed.
design:
Make the environment explicit instead of inferred.

- Pin VENV_DIR to a single default ('.venv') rather than deriving it from whichever directory exists, and keep it overridable. Decide what to do about the existing venv/ (support both for a transition, or document the rename).
- Make the venv recipe version-aware: record the interpreter used to build it (a stamp file, or read $(VENV_DIR)/bin/python --version) and rebuild when $(PYTHON) does not match, so 'make venv PYTHON=python3.12 VENV_DIR=.venv312' is the supported way to reproduce a matrix leg.
- Gate the pip install behind that stamp so lint/test/build stop hitting the network on every run; add an explicit 'make sync' or force flag for when deps genuinely changed.
- Point DEMO_MCP_COMMAND at $(PYTHON_BIN).
- If PYTHON resolves inside VENV_DIR itself (the activated-venv case), resolve it to the base interpreter or fail with a clear message rather than bootstrapping a venv from inside the venv it is replacing.

Verify by running the same make targets in both shapes: with venv activated, and in a container or fresh clone with no venv present.
acceptance_criteria: 'make venv PYTHON=<other-interpreter>' produces an environment on that interpreter even when a venv already exists, and every matrix leg from ci.yml is reproducible locally with a documented one-line command; 'make lint' and 'make test' succeed with no network access once the venv is provisioned; 'make run' launches the MCP subprocess on the venv interpreter; all four ci.yml legs stay green; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md describe the venv contract, including which directory is canonical.

title: Reconcile Python version drift: local venv 3.14 vs CI 3.11
description: Local development runs Python 3.14.6 (repo venv/bin/python, based on /opt/homebrew/bin/python3) while both GitHub Actions workflows pin python-version: 3.11 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:18, .github/workflows/publish-artifacts.yml:17). pyproject.toml declares requires-python = '>=3.11', so 3.14 is nominally in range, but nothing in CI ever exercises it. Two minor versions of drift means local green does not imply CI green (and vice versa): 3.12-3.14 removed distutils, tightened asyncio deprecations, and changed several typing behaviors this codebase touches. Decide the supported range and make CI prove it.
design: Options: (a) add a CI matrix over 3.11 + 3.14 so both the floor and the local dev version are tested; (b) pin local dev to 3.11 to match CI exactly; (c) move CI to 3.14 and raise requires-python. Recommend (a): keep requires-python '>=3.11' honest by testing the declared floor and the newest supported release, and leave publish-artifacts.yml on the floor version for the widest-compatible wheel. Verify asyncio usage in mcp_stdio.py and ws_bridge.py against 3.14 deprecations while doing this.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs the test suite on both the minimum supported Python and the version used for local development; requires-python in pyproject.toml matches the versions CI actually verifies; make lint && make test pass on every version in the matrix; CLAUDE.md's CI description is updated to reflect the matrix instead of a single 3.11 run.
close_reason: CI now runs lint/test/build across 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 (fail-fast: false); pyproject classifiers list the same four; publish-artifacts.yml documents why releases stay on the 3.11 floor; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md updated. Verified locally on all four interpreters. Follow-ups: pyacp-exl (websockets pin), pyacp-22w (bind-free integration tests).

title: Preserve MCP error codes and tool isError through the bridge
description: Two failure signals are flattened today. (1) A JSON-RPC error from the MCP server becomes MCPProtocolError(str(error)), losing the code, and ws_bridge maps every one to -32603 -- a server's -32601 and -32602 are indistinguishable to a WebSocket client. (2) A tool that fails returns a SUCCESSFUL result with isError: true; nothing inspects it (ws_bridge.py:119, :235) so the client sees ok: true. Both are wire-contract changes -- see the acp-protocol skill.

title: Honor nextCursor pagination in the MCP list wrappers
description: list_tools, list_prompts, and list_resources read only the first page of the result and drop nextCursor. Against a paginated MCP server the bridge silently reports a partial list with no error. Loop until nextCursor is absent.

title: Declare client capabilities in the MCP initialize request
description: initialize sends capabilities: {} so no conforming MCP server will ever send roots/list, elicitation/create, or sampling/createMessage -- even though _handle_server_request is wired to route them to on_server_request. Declare the capabilities we can actually answer (elicitation is the one that maps onto ACP session/request_permission; roots is plausible from session cwd/additionalDirectories; sampling must NOT be declared, there is no LLM in this runtime). Elicitation requires bumping the pinned protocol version to 2025-06-18.

title: Negotiate the MCP protocolVersion instead of ignoring the server's answer
description: MCPStdioClient.initialize sends protocolVersion 2024-11-05 and never reads the version the server returns. Per the MCP lifecycle spec a server that does not support the requested version MUST reply with one it does support, and the client SHOULD disconnect if that version is unusable. Today the handshake appears to succeed and the mismatch surfaces later as confusing failures. Compare the returned protocolVersion against what was sent and fail loudly.

title: Add an mcp-protocol skill covering the embedded MCP subprocess
description: python-acp embeds an MCP server subprocess (MCPStdioClient) but has no skill documenting the MCP wire protocol it speaks. The acp-protocol skill covers the WebSocket side only. Add a project skill covering the MCP stdio transport rules, the initialize/initialized lifecycle, capability negotiation, the client/server primitive surface, and the places where mcp_stdio.py currently diverges from the spec.
close_reason: Skill written to .claude/skills/mcp-protocol/{SKILL.md,spec-versions.md}; conventions bullet added to CLAUDE.md and mirrored to AGENTS.md; mcp_stdio.md links it; six divergences filed as pyacp-z3y/pb7/x8l/a92/ua1/k5w

title: Serialize-per-request lock blocks concurrent MCP calls
description: MCPStdioClient.request holds self._lock across both write and read, so every call is fully serialized with no pipelining. Acceptable for one server; becomes a bottleneck once multiple sessions and servers share the runtime.
close_reason: Resolved as a consequence of 7114a96: the write lock no longer spans the reply wait, so requests pipeline. Covered by test_concurrent_requests_are_all_answered

title: Add repo-docs-sync skill for co-located module docs
description: Every production .py has a co-located .md of the same basename, plus ARCHITECTURE.md mermaid diagrams and README action lists. Agents will not infer this invariant. Capture it as a skill.
close_reason: Skills written to .claude/skills/{acp-protocol,repo-docs-sync}/SKILL.md; CLAUDE.md placeholders replaced and mirrored to AGENTS.md

title: Fill in CLAUDE.md placeholder sections
description: Build & Test, Architecture Overview, and Conventions & Patterns in CLAUDE.md are still literal template text. Replace with real project content.
close_reason: Skills written to .claude/skills/{acp-protocol,repo-docs-sync}/SKILL.md; CLAUDE.md placeholders replaced and mirrored to AGENTS.md

title: Add acp-protocol skill for wire-contract rules
description: ws_bridge.py exposes two request surfaces (legacy action + JSON-RPC) with a specific error-code mapping that is not obvious from any single file. Capture the contract and the add-a-method checklist as a Claude Code skill.
close_reason: Skills written to .claude/skills/{acp-protocol,repo-docs-sync}/SKILL.md; CLAUDE.md placeholders replaced and mirrored to AGENTS.md

title: Make the two WebSocket integration tests runnable where bind() is denied
description: tests/test_mcp_stdio.py::test_websocket_bridge_lists_and_calls_tools_prompts_and_resources and ::test_websocket_bridge_handles_jsonrpc_initialize both call _free_port(), which does socket.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)). Sandboxed environments (including the one pyacp-0f6 was validated in) deny bind() for AF_INET and AF_UNIX alike, so those two tests fail with PermissionError before exercising any project code. That is 2 of 20 tests -- and specifically the only two that cover the real opening handshake and framing -- silently unavailable wherever an agent or CI runner is network-restricted.
design: Both tests can run without binding anything: pair socket.socketpair() with loop.connect_accepted_socket() for the server side and websockets.connect(uri, sock=...) for the client side. The server needs a WebSocketServer whose wrap() target stubs .sockets, .get_loop(), and .is_serving(). A working proof of this ran all of both tests' assertions unchanged on 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14 during pyacp-0f6. Options: (a) replace _free_port() with a socketpair fixture outright, (b) keep the TCP path and add a socketpair fallback when bind() raises PermissionError. Prefer (a) -- one transport path, no environment-dependent branching, and nothing about these tests actually needs a TCP port.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass in an environment where socket.bind() raises PermissionError; they still assert the same responses they do today; make lint && make test green on every version in the ci.yml matrix; if the harness moves to a shared fixture, tests/ gains no dependency the dev extra does not already provide.

title: Plan the websockets 12.0 -> 15.x upgrade off the deprecated legacy asyncio API
description: pyproject.toml pins websockets==12.0 (released Oct 2023). ws_bridge.py imports websockets.serve and websockets.server.WebSocketServerProtocol, both part of the legacy asyncio implementation that websockets 13 deprecates and 14+ moves behind websockets.legacy with a DeprecationWarning; the modern surface is websockets.asyncio.server.serve and ServerConnection. Confirmed during pyacp-0f6 that 12.0 imports clean with no warnings on 3.11-3.14, so this is not urgent -- but the pin is what makes newer interpreters safe, and it cannot be bumped without touching the bridge. Note websockets 12.0 installs the pure-Python py3-none-any wheel on 3.13/3.14 since its cp-specific wheels stop at cp312.
design: Migrate ws_bridge.py to websockets.asyncio.server: serve() returns an asyncio Server, the handler receives a ServerConnection instead of WebSocketServerProtocol, and the async-iteration and send() surface the bridge uses is unchanged. Do it as one commit that bumps the pin and rewrites the two imports plus the type annotation on _handle_client. Use the acp-protocol skill first -- _handle_client is protocol surface.
acceptance_criteria: websockets pin raised to a currently supported release; no imports from websockets.legacy or websockets.server remain in src/; make lint && make test green on every version in the ci.yml matrix; ws_bridge.md updated if the handler signature changes.

title: Send notifications/cancelled when an MCP request times out
description: request() raises MCPProtocolError after request_timeout but sends nothing to the server, which keeps working on a reply nobody will read. The spec's remedy is a notifications/cancelled carrying the requestId. Needs a mock_mcp_server.py branch that reports what it received.

title: Close the subprocess stdin before SIGTERM in MCPStdioClient.stop
description: The MCP stdio shutdown sequence is: close the server's stdin, wait for exit, SIGTERM, wait, SIGKILL. stop() starts at terminate(), so servers that exit cleanly on EOF get signalled instead of shutting down normally.
